questions.prompt: Which learning type uses inputs without labels, for example grouping customers by behaviour?
questions.explanation: Unsupervised learning finds structure without labels (k-means, PCA).

options: Self-supervised learning: predicting the next token over large text collections
questions.explanation: Labels come from the data itself (the next token); then supervised fine-tuning and preference methods adapt the model to follow instructions.

questions.prompt: Classic ML such as fraud detection and forecasting is still widely used alongside generative AI.
questions.explanation: True. Thinking AI means only chatbots is a listed mistake.

questions.prompt: A spam filter that labels incoming email is what kind of model?
questions.explanation: Discriminative models predict a label or number from an input; generative models produce new samples.

questions.prompt: Which role's main question is 'Is there a better method?'
questions.explanation: Scientists advance methods with hypotheses, controlled experiments and papers. Engineers ask 'can we ship it reliably?', test engineers 'can we trust it?'.

questions.prompt: A job ad titled 'AI Engineer' lists responsibilities: design eval datasets, run red-team tests, calibrate LLM judges. How should you read it?
options: Read responsibilities, not titles: this is mostly AI test engineering work
questions.explanation: Companies use titles differently; treating them as fixed is a listed mistake.

questions.prompt: A team spends months picking the best model but has no evaluation set, no monitoring and unclear success metrics. What will most likely decide whether the product works?
options: Problem framing, data quality, evaluation and monitoring across the lifecycle
questions.explanation: Focusing only on the model is a listed mistake; the lifecycle stages decide success.

questions.prompt: Which artefacts belong to the problem-framing and data stages? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Registry entries belong to deployment. Framing produces success metrics and risk assessment; the data stage produces datasets and data cards.

questions.prompt: A developer jumps straight to calling LLM APIs and tweaks prompts by feel. Why does the lesson call skipping foundations a mistake?
options: Without understanding evaluation they cannot tell whether a change helped or hurt
questions.explanation: Evaluation literacy is foundational for every role in the track.
